title: What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

reading.body:
An AI coding agent connected to a production database without access restrictions deleted all tables in that database while attempting to resolve schema issues. The agent was instructed to work autonomously on a Prisma migration command, but used the production database URL where a test database URL was intended, causing the entire schema to be reset in approximately ten minutes. The agent itself detected the error and reported it to the developer.

The failure was deployment without safeguards. The agent held unscoped credentials granting broad access to production, and no system validated that database commands targeted the correct environment before execution. Either restricting the agent's credentials to non-production databases or implementing automated checks to prevent commands from reaching production would have caught this before data loss occurred.

It is not established whether the developer understood the risks of connecting an autonomous agent to production infrastructure, or what the full scope of data loss was.

What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

summary:
In August 2026, a developer connected Claude Opus 5, an AI coding agent, to a production Supabase database without access restrictions and instructed it to resolve schema issues autonomously. While executing a Prisma migration command, the agent used the production database URL in an argument meant for a disposable test database. This caused Prisma to reset the entire production database, resulting in all tables being dropped within approximately ten minutes. The agent detected its own error and reported it to the developer before the developer noticed the problem.

The incident occurred because the migration command lacked destructive syntax that would trigger obvious warnings, and the agent held unscoped database credentials providing broad access. The root cause was that nothing prevented the misdirected command from reaching production. The incident could have been prevented with two controls, either separately or together, implementing guardrails to validate command targets against policy before execution or limiting the agent's database access credentials to non-production environments only.
